subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond shipped /tools/invoke, tools.invoke, SDK, and command-cron paths, and what owner/config/security gates are required for host filesystem, exec, slash/CLI, and cron tool-call payloads?
rationale: Current main implements the safe single-tool gateway slice, but the remaining requested surfaces intentionally change privileged execution and operator control boundaries.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker and accept only focused PRs with maintainer-reviewed owner checks, config gates, docs, tests, and real behavior/security proof.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK direct invoke and command cron sufficient for now, then close or reject host-FS, exec, slash/CLI, and cron tool-call expansion until a maintainer-sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve a broader direct execution design
options.body: Allow a larger core design only after maintainers define the security model, operator controls, audit behavior, and migration story up front.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker and accept only focused PRs with maintainer-reviewed owner checks, config gates, docs, tests, and real behavior/security proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily a product/security boundary for privileged gateway execution rather than a mechanical code follow-up.
